relevance_note: The paper re-analyses 89 patients with A20 haploinsufficiency, each with an individual-level row and TNFAIP3 variant in Table S1: 'The remaining 89 patients from 39 families were reported with heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read only the paper, schema, rules and instructions. Table S1 (supplementary file Data_Sheet_2.PDF) gives one row per patient: Family (Ref.), amino-acid alteration, patient number, AOS, gender and +/- columns for RF, oral ulcers, genital ulcers, ocular, skin lesion, vasculitis, GI ulcers, MSD, AITD, RRTI, plus 'Other manifestations', 'Initial diagnosis' and 'Treatment'. I transcribed it by hand (no script). The Table S1 legend (line 'AOS: age of onset, RF: recurrent fever, GI: gastrointestinal, MSD: musculoskeletal disorder, AITD: autoimmune thyroid disorder, RRTI: recurrent respiratory tract infection, F:female, M:male, BD: Behcer's disease, ...') defines the abbreviations and F/M but does NOT define '+' and '-'. Per the v3/v6 table-symbol rule I therefore treat a '+' cell as observed (the paper's Table 1 reports the same features as percentages for the same 89 patients, and my '+' count for the recurrent-fever column, 37, equals the 37/89 printed there, which supports '+' = present and fixes the column order) but a '-' cell as 'not reported', not 'excluded'; I emit no excluded rows from '-' cells. Counting the oral-ulcer column gives me more '+' cells than the 62/89 printed in Table 1, so the two tables do not agree exactly on that feature; I kept the per-patient cells as printed. I did not verify every column total, so the Table 1 numerators are not used as evidence anywhere. Rows are labelled 'Table S1 #<patient number>' (bare numbers under the 'Patient' heading, v4 rule). source_reference_in_review is the reference number printed in the 'Family (Ref.)' cell, which indexes the reference list of the supplementary file (checked: (1) Shigemura/C243Y, (2) Kadowaki, (16) Shimizu/exon 2-3 deletion). Cells that continue on following lines are quoted as a list of contiguous fragments; I never joined non-contiguous text. Stacked-cell warning: in Table S2 of the supplement each cell holds one value per mutation locus (column of counts), and the Table S2 rows list 1-3 values separated by ' / ' in some 'Other manifestations'/'Treatment' cells; nothing was assigned by position. The legend's 'Behcer's disease' and the split words ('insulin-dependent' / 'diabetes', 'Aortic valve insufficie' / 'ncy') are printed that way in the converted file; spans keep that. Uncertainties: the initial diagnosis of each patient (Table S1 column) and the p.Leu227* / p.Phe224Serfs*4 onset analysis (Figure S1, Table S2) are group-level and are not represented by a schema field; no patient is called a proband, so is_proband is false throughout with span null; zygosity 'heterozygous' and pathogenicity 'loss-of-function' come from the cohort-level sentence naming the 89 patients. The paper's Methods text cites its sources as (5, 8, 10-12) while the Table S1 'Family (Ref.)' cell numbers (1)-(21) match the supplementary file's own reference list, not the main list; I copied the cell values verbatim. Table S1 numbers patients 1-89 but its family column runs to 41 while the text says 39 families, and family numbers 31 and 32 do not appear; I did not invent rows for them. The 'Other manifestations', 'Initial diagnosis' and 'Treatment' cells of Table S1 are wrapped across several lines in the converted Markdown, so I quote them as lists of contiguous fragments and never join non-contiguous text.

study_type.span: We reviewed the HA20 cases in previous literature and summarized the clinical features, TNFAIP3 mutation loci and the disrupted domains caused by different sites and patterns of mutations.

n_patients_reported.span: The remaining 89 patients from 39 families were reported with heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 (Table S1)

cohort_size_as_stated.span: We initially collected a total of 93 cases according to the inclusion criteria and 4 patients were excluded from the study due to the presence of additional mutations.
